sections.label: COSMIC platform for sharing financial crime information
sections.summary: MAS proposes COSMIC, a secure digital platform for FIs to share information on customers with multiple red flags, and the Bill amends the Financial Services and Markets Act 2022 to permit this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: To address this problem, MAS proposes to establish and maintain a secure digital platform for FIs to share, with one another, information on customers who exhibit multiple "red flags" that may indicate potential financial crime concerns, if stipulated thresholds are met.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: These include those who seek to be or have been a customer of an FI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: This platform will be named COSMIC, which is short for "Collaborative Sharing of ML/TF Information and Cases".

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: The Bill amends the Financial Services and Markets Act 2022 to permit this sharing of information and provides the legal framework for it.

sections.label: First phase COSMIC rollout
sections.summary: In the first phase, MAS will make COSMIC available to the six major Singapore banks it is co-developing the platform with.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: In the first phase, MAS will make COSMIC available to the six major Singapore banks which it is already co-developing the platform with.

sections.label: Bill sets out information sharing modes
sections.summary: The Bill sets out how information may be shared and the types of serious cases warranting sharing, with three modes of sharing via COSMIC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: The Bill will set out how this information may be shared, and the types of cases that are serious enough to warrant such sharing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: There are three modes under the Bill in which information may be shared via COSMIC.

sections.label: Thresholds and red flags directive
sections.summary: Thresholds are progressively higher for Request, Provide and Alert, and MAS will issue a directive detailing threshold criteria and associated red flags for each mode.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: The thresholds are progressively higher for Request, Provide and then, finally, Alert.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: To establish an objective standard for when information may be shared under each of these three modes of sharing, MAS will issue a directive to participant FIs detailing the threshold criteria for each of them and the list of "red flags" associated with each threshold.

sections.label: Immunity for disclosures on COSMIC
sections.summary: They will be granted immunity from liability for loss arising from disclosure on COSMIC if done in accordance with the legal framework, with reasonable care and in good faith.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: Specifically, they will be granted immunity from liability for any loss arising out of the disclosure on COSMIC, or any act or omission in consequence of the disclosure, if the disclosure was done in accordance with the legal framework, with reasonable care and in good faith.

sections.label: Restrictions and cybersecurity for COSMIC data
sections.summary: Participant FIs cannot disclose COSMIC information to third parties except in specified circumstances, and MAS can require strong cybersecurity measures for COSMIC data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: When information is passed to participant FIs, participant FIs will not be allowed to disclose information obtained from COSMIC to a third party, except in tightly circumscribed and specified circumstances, such as for compliance with Court orders or requests from Police to facilitate investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Bill will empower MAS to require participant FIs to maintain strong information cybersecurity measures for COSMIC data.

sections.label: MAS and STRO platform access
sections.summary: MAS will access all information shared on the platform, and STRO can view and use COSMIC information to support financial crime prevention and detection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: Apart from participant FIs, MAS will have access to all information shared on the platform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
sentences.text: STRO, which analyses and disseminates financial intelligence to law enforcement and regulatory agencies, will also be able to view and use COSMIC information to support the prevention and detection of financial crime.

sections.label: Overcoming FI information sharing limits
sections.summary: The COSMIC platform addresses FIs' limited ability to share information caused by client confidentiality obligations and banking secrecy regulations, enabling stronger public-private partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This capitalises on the limited ability of FIs to share and piece information together, in part due to the FIs' compliance with well-intentioned client confidentiality obligations as well as banking secrecy regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to overcome this, and I believe the new digital COSMIC platform paves the way forward for stronger public-private partnerships, for authorities and FIs to assess risks more holistically and disrupt financial crime more effectively.

sections.label: Scam losses and COSMIC
sections.summary: Close to S$1.3 billion was lost to scams over two years, and the Minister is asked to clarify if and how COSMIC can help stem scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Close to S$1.3 billion have been lost to scams over the last two years, despite the best efforts of authorities and private sector entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given significant impact, can the Minister clarify if and how COSMIC can help to stem this facilitation of scams?

sections.label: Accountability in cybersecurity incidents
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify the roles and responsibilities of the participating FI providing information versus MAS as COSMIC platform owner in a cybersecurity incident or breach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For clearer accountability, can the Minister clarify the roles and responsibilities of the participating FI who provides the information, vis-à-vis MAS as the owner of the COSMIC platform, in the unfortunate event of a cybersecurity incident or breach?

sections.label: Collaboration and Singapore's reputation
sections.summary: Greater collaboration between FIs and authorities is fostered so criminal operations can be unravelled quickly, strengthening oversight of Singapore's reputation as a global financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Greater collaboration between FIs and authorities is fostered, so that as sophisticated as criminal operations may be, they can be quickly unravelled and have fewer places to hide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This will further strengthen the oversight of Singapore's reputation as a global financial centre.

sections.label: MAS COSMIC platform for red flags
sections.summary: MAS plans to establish and maintain a secure digital platform called COSMIC for FIs to share information on customers exhibiting multiple red flags of potential illicit activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address this gap, MAS plans to establish and maintain a secure digital platform for FIs called COSMIC to share information on customers that exhibit multiple "red flags" indicative of potential illicit activities with one another.

sections.label: Smaller banks and AML enforcement
sections.summary: MAS withdrew Falcon Private Bank and BSI Bank licences in 2016 and fined Bank J Safra Sarasin in 2021 for AML/CFT lapses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In comparison, it is the smaller offshore and private banks that would, perhaps, benefit more from such a network of information sharing and provide the most insight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And to exemplify this, MAS withdrew the merchant banking license of one such FI, Falcon Private Bank Ltd, in 2016, as well as another BSI Bank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2021, MAS fined a Singapore branch of another such FI, Bank J Safra Sarasin Ltd, for Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance lapses.

sections.label: MAS initial phase duration
sections.summary: MAS said in its consultation response that the initial phase would last as long as two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After all, in its response to the consultation with FIs, MAS said that the initial phase would last as long as two years, which is a fairly long time.

sections.label: Bill thresholds and red flags
sections.summary: The Bill permits information sharing only when behaviour or transactions cross stipulated red flag thresholds, which appear static.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Bill, information sharing will only be permitted if the customer's behaviour or transaction activities exhibit predetermined "red flags" that cross stipulated thresholds, suggesting that potential financial crime could be taking place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The wording in the Bill seems to suggest that these thresholds are static thresholds without the element for dynamic adjustment, which is at odds with the global environment's dynamic pace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask the Government: firstly, how often will these thresholds be reviewed to determine if these thresholds have been set to effectively identify illicit financial flows?

sections.label: COSMIC compromise and responsibility
sections.summary: If COSMIC or its information is compromised, the outcome may be harmful for FIs, customers and Singapore's reputation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should the system, or some, or all of the information that it contains fall prey to bad actors, or if COSMIC is compromised, the outcome may be extremely harmful for FIs, their customers and for Singapore reputationally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Who will be responsible for the integrity of the system?

sections.label: Disclosing FI discretion timing
sections.summary: Under proposed section 28D, the disclosing FI has discretion whether to disclose sought risk information to the requesting FI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: On operational issues, I seek clarification on the important timing issue between the requesting FI and the disclosing FI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This addresses the question, "Do you have a piece?" I note that under the proposed section 28D of the Bill, the disclosing FI has a discretion whether to disclose to the requesting FI the risk information that is being sought for.

sections.label: Six major banks' AML capabilities
sections.summary: The six major commercial banks chosen to join COSMIC all have strong AML/CFT capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Currently, the six major commercial banks chosen to join COSMIC all have strong AML/CFT capabilities.

sections.label: Expanding MAS list considerations
sections.summary: MAS would consider how to prevent FIs with less compliance capabilities from unfairly leveraging off other FIs if the list is expanded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Going forward, should MAS decide to expand the list to include more FIs, what would be the considerations to ensure that FIs which have less compliance capabilities and capacities do not unfairly leverage off FIs which do?

sections.label: Compulsory minimum compliance competencies
sections.summary: One option is to make it compulsory for all FIs licensed in Singapore to eventually have a minimum level of compliance competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: One possible option is to make it compulsory for all FIs licensed in Singapore to eventually have a minimum level of compliance competencies so that they all meet the entry requirements.

sections.label: Section 28J risk information offence
sections.summary: The Bill proposes under section 28J an offence for a prescribed FI or its officers knowingly or recklessly disclosing false or misleading risk information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: First, it is proposed that under section 28J in the Bill that a prescribed FI or its officers who knowingly or recklessly discloses, or publishes any risk information pertaining to a customer of the bank that is false or misleading in a material particular.

sections.label: Lower probity standard questioned
sections.summary: The proposed information-sharing framework changes the paradigm, and the speaker questions allowing a lower standard of probity despite substantially the same repercussion on customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The proposed information-sharing framework between FIs changes the paradigm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I am struggling to understand why in the new paradigm, we are allowing for a lower standard of probity on the part of the FIs when, in fact, the repercussion on the customer is substantially the same.

sections.label: Listing offences in Sixth Schedule
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the proposed offences against FIs under the information-sharing framework be considered for listing in the Sixth Schedule of the CPC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Next, I would like to suggest that the proposed offences against FIs under the information-sharing framework be considered for listing in the Sixth Schedule of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) under the Minister's powers provided for under section 427(1) of the CPC.

sections.label: Including offences in Sixth Schedule
sections.summary: The speaker believes there is a case for including the proposed offences under the Bill into the Sixth Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Given that the proposed offences under the Bill also involve the same subject matter, I believe there is a case for including these offences into the Sixth Schedule.

sections.label: Pangolin scales and ivory seizures
sections.summary: Singapore seized 12.9 tonnes of pangolin scales from Nigeria and 8.8 tonnes of ivory from about 300 elephants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: In April 2019, we broke the record by finding 12.9 tonnes of pangolin scales being smuggled in a shipment from Nigeria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: This was worth over $50 million and cost the lives of over 17,000 pangolins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Three months after that, we seized a shipment of 8.8 tonnes of ivory, estimated to come from nearly 300 African elephants.

sections.label: Wildlife crime red flags
sections.summary: The question asks whether MAS will include wildlife crime links in the scope of identified red flags.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As MAS develops this platform, will MAS consider including in the scope of the "red flags" identified to those associated with wildlife crime?

sections.label: Bill and bank data laws
sections.summary: The question asks whether the new Bill overrides the Banking Secrecy Act and PDPA so six banks can share information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will this new Bill override the regulations stated in the Banking Secrecy Act and the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA) so that these six banks can share information with one another?

sections.label: MAS and COSMIC subscription
sections.summary: The question asks why MAS cannot require all banks, especially private banks, to subscribe to COSMIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Along the same vein, why can MAS not request all banks, especially private banks, to subscribe to COSMIC?

sections.label: US banks in COSMIC
sections.summary: The speaker urges MAS to include Singaporean branches of US banks like JP Morgan, Wells Fargo and Bank of New York in COSMIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Many international trade transactions are settled in United States (US) dollars and the bulk of US dollar remittances are cleared through US banks like JP Morgan, Wells Fargo and Bank of New York.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge MAS to include Singaporean branches of the abovementioned US banks to participate in COSMIC.

sections.label: COSMIC setup cost and funding
sections.summary: The question asks how much COSMIC costs to set up and whether MAS is funding its development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How much does it cost to set up COSMIC and is MAS funding the development of this system?

sections.label: Benefits for banks joining COSMIC
sections.summary: A question asks what benefits banks get from joining COSMIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mdm Deputy Speaker, what are the benefits for banks to join COSMIC?

sections.label: Red flags and thresholds listing
sections.summary: The Bill permits information sharing only when customer behaviour or transactions show predetermined red flags crossing stipulated thresholds, and asks if these will be listed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill states that information sharing will only be permitted if the customer's behaviour or transaction activities exhibit predetermined "red flags" that cross stipulated thresholds, suggesting that potential financial crime could be taking place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the predetermined "red flags" and thresholds be listed?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Specifically, it provides the necessary groundwork for the Act to include not just banks incorporated in Singapore.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Command stakeholder network
sections.summary: The Anti-Scam Command works with over 80 stakeholders to freeze suspected scam accounts, recover funds and mitigate victims' losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Singapore Police Force's Anti-Scam Command collaborates with a network of more than 80 stakeholders, comprising FIs, fintechs, telecommunication companies and online marketplaces, to swiftly freeze bank accounts suspected of scams, recover funds and mitigate losses suffered by victims.

sections.label: Man sentenced for scam companies
sections.summary: A Singaporean man was sentenced to six weeks' imprisonment and disqualified as a director for five years for helping set up four companies receiving scam proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For example, late last year, a Singaporean man was sentenced to six weeks' imprisonment and disqualified from being a director for five years, for assisting to set up four companies that were used to receive scam proceeds from multiple local and overseas victims.

sections.label: MAS back-testing for COSMIC
sections.summary: MAS conducted back-testing of potential ML/TF/PF cases with participant FIs during COSMIC's development to refine red flags and threshold criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On Mr Goh's question as to whether any back-testing has been done on past cases that COSMIC could have detected, MAS had, indeed, conducted back-testing of potential ML/TF/PF cases with participant FIs as COSMIC was being developed, and this is to refine the high-risk indicators or, as I mentioned, "red flags", and also our threshold criteria.

sections.label: Sharing despite legal restrictions
sections.summary: Participant FIs may share COSMIC risk information as permitted under the Bill despite restrictions imposed by any written law or contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Participant FIs may share COSMIC risk information as permitted under the Bill despite any restrictions that may be imposed by any written law or contract.

sections.label: MAS Notice 626 personal data
sections.summary: Paragraph 13.4 of MAS Notice 626 lets a bank collect personal data, itself or via a third party, to comply with Notice 626.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To clarify Mr Leon Perera's query, paragraph 13.4 of the MAS Notice 626 allows a bank to collect personal data, whether by itself or through a third party, for the purposes of complying with the requirements of Notice 626, for example, in the conduct of customer due diligence.

sections.label: Two-year voluntary sharing period
sections.summary: An initial two-year voluntary sharing period gives participant FIs time to familiarise with information-sharing and the COSMIC platform to achieve operational stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This will ensure that sharing is purposeful and that legitimate customers are not unduly affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This initial two-year period of voluntary sharing is to allow participant FIs adequate time to familiarise themselves with the new information-sharing paradigm and also for the COSMIC platform, which will be integrated with the FIs' systems, so as to achieve operational stability.

sections.label: Mandatory sharing on COSMIC
sections.summary: MAS intends to eventually make sharing mandatory on COSMIC and has set agreed service timelines with participant FIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Eventually, we intend to make such sharing mandatory on COSMIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS has established with the participant FIs a set of agreed upon service timelines.

sections.label: MAS owns COSMIC platform
sections.summary: MAS owns the COSMIC platform, bears infrastructure development costs as a public good, and participating banks pay no subscription fee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS is the owner of the COSMIC platform and will bear the costs of developing the infrastructure, which we view as serving a public good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Participating banks would not have to pay a subscription fee.

sections.label: False disclosure offence section 28J
sections.summary: Under new section 28J, a participant FI or its officer knowingly or recklessly making a false or misleading disclosure on COSMIC is guilty of an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As Mr Murali Pillai has pointed out, under the new section 28J, a participant FI or an officer of the FIs that knowingly or recklessly makes a false or misleading disclosure on COSMIC will be guilty of an offence.

sections.label: STRO access to COSMIC information
sections.summary: Apart from MAS, STRO is the only agency with direct access to COSMIC information to fulfil its role as Singapore's financial intelligence unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Given the potential sensitivity of COSMIC information, STRO is the only agency, apart from MAS, that will have direct access to COSMIC information to help fulfil its role as Singapore's financial intelligence unit.

sections.label: COSMIC disclosure within financial groups
sections.summary: FIs on COSMIC may disclose received information within their financial group for group-wide ML/TF/PF risk management, on a need-to-know basis, with safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In line with this principle, FIs participating on COSMIC will also be permitted to disclose the information they receive from COSMIC within their financial group, only for group-wide ML/TF/PF risk management purposes, on a need-to-know basis, provided additional safeguards set out in the legislation are in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This is to mitigate the risks of leakage, and unauthorised disclosures and unintended legal risks to FIs that had shared the information.
